title.zh: 卷二百八十九 列傳第四十八 高瓊 范廷召 葛霸
title.en: Volume 289 Biographies 48: Gao Qiong, Fan Tingzhao, Ge Ba
title.raw: 卷二百八十九 列傳第四十八 高瓊 范廷召 葛霸 Volume 289 Biographies 48: Gao Qiong, Fan Tingzhao, Ge Ba

sentences.zh: 高瓊，家世燕人。

translations.literal: Gao Qiong — his family for generations were men of Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Qiong came from a family originally of Yan.

sentences.zh: 祖霸，父乾。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Ba; his father was Qian.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Ba, and his father was Qian.

sentences.zh: 五代時，李景據江南，潛結契丹，歲遣單使往復。

translations.literal: During the Five Dynasties, Li Jing held the lands south of the Yangtze, secretly allied with the Khitan, and each year sent lone envoys back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: During the Five Dynasties, Li Jing held sway over the lands south of the Yangtze. He secretly allied himself with the Khitan and each year dispatched lone envoys to and fro.

sentences.zh: 霸將契丹之命，以乾從行使景。

translations.literal: Ba received the Khitan commission and took Qian along as attendant on the embassy to Jing.
translations.idiomatic: Ba was entrusted with the Khitan mission and brought Qian along as his attendant on the embassy to Li Jing.

sentences.zh: 方至江左，諜間北使與中夏構隙，以紓疆場之難，遂殺霸，居乾濠州，聲言為汴人所殺。

translations.literal: Just as they reached the Jiang-Zuo region, spies sowed discord between the northern envoys and the Central State to ease frontier difficulties; they then killed Ba, detained Qian in Haozhou, and claimed he had been killed by men of Bian.
translations.idiomatic: When they had just reached the south, Li Jing's agents exploited tensions between the northern envoys and the Central State to relieve frontier pressure. Ba was killed, Qian was detained in Haozhou, and the court publicly declared that the envoy had been murdered by men from Bian.

sentences.zh: 乾在濠州生三子，以江左蹙弱，尋挈族歸中朝，給田亳州之蒙城，因土著焉。

translations.literal: Qian bore three sons in Haozhou; because the Jiang-Zuo was weak and constricted, he soon brought his clan back to the Central Court, was granted fields in Mengcheng of Bozhou, and settled there as natives.
translations.idiomatic: While detained in Haozhou, Qian had three sons. Finding the south increasingly enfeebled, he eventually brought his entire clan back to the Central Court, received land grants in Mengcheng, Bozhou, and settled there permanently.

sentences.zh: 瓊少勇鷙無賴，為盜，事敗，將磔於市，暑雨創潰，伺守者稍怠，即掣釘而遁。

translations.literal: Qiong in youth was fierce and unruly; he became a bandit, and when the affair failed he was to be dismembered in the market. Summer rain caused his wounds to fester; when the guards slackened slightly, he pulled out the nails and escaped.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Qiong was fierce, truculent, and without restraint. He took to banditry, and when caught he was sentenced to public dismemberment. Summer rains made his wounds suppurate; when his guards relaxed their vigilance even slightly, he tore free the nails holding him and escaped.

sentences.zh: 事王審琦，太宗尹京邑，知其材勇，召置帳下。

translations.literal: He served Wang Shenqi. When the Taizong administered the capital district, knowing his talent and bravery, he summoned and placed him under his command.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the service of Wang Shenqi. When Prince Taizong governed the capital district and learned of his courage and ability, he summoned Qiong and placed him in his personal retinue.

sentences.zh: 太宗嘗侍宴禁中，甚醉，及退，太祖送至苑門。

translations.literal: Taizong once attended a banquet in the palace and became very drunk; when he withdrew, Taizu escorted him to the garden gate.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion Taizong attended a palace banquet and became thoroughly intoxicated. When he took his leave, Taizu escorted him as far as the garden gate.

sentences.zh: 時瓊與戴興、王超、李斌、桑讚從，瓊左手執靮，右手執鐙，太宗乃能乘馬。

translations.literal: At the time Qiong followed with Dai Xing, Wang Chao, Li Bin, and Sang Zan; Qiong held the bridle in his left hand and the stirrup in his right, and only then could Taizong mount his horse.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was among those accompanying him—along with Dai Xing, Wang Chao, Li Bin, and Sang Zan. Qiong held the bridle in his left hand and the stirrup in his right, enabling the prince to mount.

sentences.zh: 太祖顧瓊等壯之，因賜以控鶴官衣帶及器帛，且勖令盡心焉。

translations.literal: Taizu looked at Qiong and the others, admiring their sturdy bearing, and so bestowed upon them the robes, belts, and accoutrements of the Crane-Controlling Guard, urging them to serve with full devotion.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu looked over Qiong and his companions, impressed by their sturdy bearing, and rewarded them with the robes, belts, and equipment of the Crane-Controlling Guard, urging them to serve with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 會有龍騎亡命卒數十人，因知州臧丙出郊，謀劫其導從以叛。

translations.literal: It happened that several dozen deserters from the Dragon Cavalry, taking advantage of Prefect Zang Bing going out to the suburbs, plotted to seize his escort and rebel.
translations.idiomatic: Several dozen deserters from the Dragon Cavalry learned that Prefect Zang Bing was traveling in the countryside and plotted to ambush his escort and rebel.

sentences.zh: 瓊聞即白丙，趣還城，因自率從卒數十人，挾弓矢單騎追捕，至榆林村，及之。

translations.literal: Upon hearing this, Qiong immediately informed Bing and urged him to hurry back to the city; then he personally led several dozen followers, bearing bow and arrows, and pursued alone on horseback to Yulin Village, where he caught up with them.
translations.idiomatic: Upon hearing this, Qiong immediately warned Zang Bing and urged him to hurry back to the city. He then personally led several dozen followers, armed with bow and arrows, riding alone in pursuit until he overtook the rebels at Yulin Village.

sentences.zh: 賊入村後舍，登牆以拒。

translations.literal: The bandits entered a rear dwelling in the village, climbed the wall, and resisted.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels fled into a rear building in the village and climbed onto the wall to make a stand.

sentences.zh: 賊首青腳狼者注弩將射瓊，瓊引弓一發斃之，遂悉擒送於州。

translations.literal: The bandit chieftain called Blue-Footed Wolf drew his crossbow intending to shoot Qiong; Qiong drew his bow, fired once, and killed him; then he captured all of them and sent them to the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Their leader, known as Blue-Footed Wolf, nocked an arrow to shoot Qiong. Qiong drew his bow, loosed a single shot, and killed him on the spot. He then captured the entire band and delivered them to the prefectural authorities.

sentences.zh: 丙上其事。

translations.literal: Bing reported the affair upward.
translations.idiomatic: Zang Bing reported the incident to his superiors.

sentences.zh: 會將北伐，召歸。

translations.literal: When a northern campaign was about to be launched, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When a northern expedition was being planned, he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 授馬步軍都軍頭、領薊州刺史、樓船戰棹都指揮使，步船千艘赴雄州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Cavalry and Infantry, concurrently Prefect of Jizhou and Commander of War Ships and Battle Oars, and with a thousand infantry ships proceeded to Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed commander-in-chief of cavalry and infantry, given concurrent duties as prefect of Jizhou and commander of the war fleet, and dispatched with a thousand transport ships to Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 又城易州。

translations.literal: He also fortified Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also undertook the fortification of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 師還，為天武右廂都指揮使、領本州團練使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he became Commander of the Right Wing of the Celestial Martial Guard and concurrently Military Commissioner of his native prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned, he was made commander of the Right Wing of the Celestial Martial Guard and concurrently military commissioner of his home prefecture.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，遷左廂，改領富州團練使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Duangong reign, he was transferred to the Left Wing and changed to concurrently serve as Military Commissioner of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era he was transferred to the Left Wing and reassigned as military commissioner of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 是秋，出為單州防禦使，改貝州部署。

translations.literal: That autumn he went out as Defense Commissioner of Shanzhou and was reassigned to command at Beizhou.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he was posted as defense commissioner of Shanzhou, then reassigned to command the garrison at Beizhou.

sentences.zh: 其出守也，與范廷召、王超、孔守正並命焉。

translations.literal: When he went out to garrison, he was appointed together with Fan Tingzhao, Wang Chao, and Kong Shouzheng.
translations.idiomatic: His frontier posting came at the same time as comparable appointments for Fan Tingzhao, Wang Chao, and Kong Shouzheng.

sentences.zh: 數月，廷召等皆復補兵職，瓊頗悒悒。

translations.literal: Several months later, Tingzhao and the others were all restored to military posts, and Qiong was rather despondent.
translations.idiomatic: Within a few months Fan Tingzhao and the others had all been restored to military command, while Qiong remained in his lesser post and grew increasingly despondent.

sentences.zh: 時王承衍鎮貝丘，公主每入禁中，頗知上於瓊厚，承衍每寬慰之。

translations.literal: At the time Wang Chengyan garrisoned Beiqiu; the princess, each time she entered the palace, knew well the emperor's favor toward Qiong, and Chengyan often comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Chengyan was then stationed at Beiqiu. His wife, a princess who frequently visited the palace, was well aware of the emperor's high regard for Qiong, and Chengyan often reassured him on that account.

sentences.zh: 二年，召還。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the reign he was recalled to court.

sentences.zh: 故事，廉察以上入朝，始有茶藥之賜，至是特賜瓊焉。

translations.literal: By precedent, only inspectors and above received gifts of tea and medicine upon entering court; on this occasion Qiong was specially granted them.
translations.idiomatic: By custom only officials of inspector rank and above received gifts of tea and medicine when summoned to court; on this occasion Qiong was granted them as an exceptional honor.

sentences.zh: 三月，遷朔、易帥臣，制授瓊侍衛步軍都指揮使、領歸義軍節度，廷召輩始加觀察使，不得與瓊比。

translations.literal: In the third month the commanders of Shuozhou and Yizhou were changed; Qiong was appointed Commander of the Palace Guard Infantry and concurrently Military Governor of the Guiyi Army; Tingzhao and his group were only then given Observation Commissioner titles, unable to compare with Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month the commanders for Shuozhou and Yizhou were reshuffled. Qiong was appointed commander of the Palace Guard Infantry and given the concurrent title of military governor of the Guiyi Army. Fan Tingzhao and his peers received only observation commissioner ranks—positions that could not compare with Qiong's.

sentences.zh: 出為幷州馬步軍都部署，時潘美亦在太原，舊制，節度使領軍職者居上，瓊以美舊臣，表請居其下，從之。

translations.literal: He went out as Overall Commander of Cavalry and Infantry at Bingzhou; at the time Pan Mei was also at Taiyuan. By old regulation, a military governor who held a military command ranked above; Qiong, considering Mei a veteran minister, submitted a memorial requesting to rank below him, and this was granted.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as overall commander of cavalry and infantry at Bingzhou. Pan Mei was then stationed at Taiyuan as well. By established custom a military governor who held a field command outranked a mere deployment commander, but Qiong, respecting Mei as a senior officer of the founding era, petitioned to serve under him, and the request was granted.

sentences.zh: 戍兵有以廩食陳腐嘩言者，瓊知之，一日，出巡諸營，士卒方聚食，因取其飯自啖之，謂眾曰：「今邊鄙無警，爾等坐飽甘豐，宜知幸也。

translations.literal: Among the garrison troops there were those who clamored about stale and rotten grain rations; Qiong learned of this. One day, while inspecting the camps, the soldiers were just gathering to eat; he took some of their food and ate it himself, saying to the crowd: "Now the frontier is untroubled; you sit and eat your fill of good provisions—you should know your good fortune."
translations.idiomatic: Some garrison troops had been grumbling that their grain rations were stale and rotten. Learning of this, Qiong one day made the rounds of the camps while the men were at their meal. He took a portion of their food and ate it himself, then told the assembled soldiers: "The frontier is at peace. You sit here eating your fill of good provisions—you ought to count yourselves fortunate."

sentences.zh: 」眾言遂息。

translations.literal: The clamor then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: The grumbling then ceased.

sentences.zh: 改鎮州都部署。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Overall Commander at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as overall commander at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 至道中，就改保大軍節度，典軍如故。

translations.literal: During the Zhidao era he was concurrently made Military Governor of the Baoda Army, continuing to command troops as before.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era he was given the concurrent title of military governor of the Baoda Army while continuing his military duties as before.

sentences.zh: 真宗即位，加彰信軍節度，充太宗山陵部署，復為幷代都部署。

translations.literal: When Zhenzong ascended the throne, Qiong was additionally made Military Governor of the Zhangxin Army, appointed overseer of Taizong's tomb, and again made Overall Commander of Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhenzong ascended the throne, Qiong received the additional title of military governor of the Zhangxin Army, was appointed overseer of Taizong's imperial tomb, and was again made overall commander of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 咸平中，契丹犯塞，其母車帳至狼山大夏。

translations.literal: During the Xianping era the Khitan raided the frontier; the empress dowager's camp reached Langshan and Daxia.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianping era the Khitan invaded the frontier, and the empress dowager's own camp advanced as far as Langshan and Daxia.

sentences.zh: 上親巡河朔，遣楊允恭馳往，召瓊率所部出土門，與石保吉會鎮、定。

translations.literal: The emperor personally toured Hebei and dispatched Yang Yonggong posthaste to summon Qiong to lead his forces out through Tumen and join Shi Baoji at Zhen and Ding.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally toured Hebei and dispatched Yang Yonggong posthaste to summon Qiong, ordering him to lead his troops out through Tumen and rendezvous with Shi Baoji at Zhen and Ding.

sentences.zh: 既而傅潛以逗留得罪，即召瓊代之。

translations.literal: Soon afterward Fu Qian was punished for delay, and Qiong was summoned to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: Fu Qian was soon punished for his delay in advancing, and Qiong was summoned to replace him.

sentences.zh: 兵罷，復還本任。

translations.literal: When the campaign ended, he returned to his original post.
translations.idiomatic: When the campaign ended, he returned to his previous post.

sentences.zh: 轉運使言其政績，詔褒之。

translations.literal: The transport commissioner reported his administrative achievements, and an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: The transport commissioner reported on his administrative achievements, and the emperor issued an edict praising him.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，代還，以手創不任持笏，詔執梃入謁，授殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping, upon returning from his frontier tour of duty, because a wound to his hand prevented him from holding the audience tablet, an edict permitted him to enter audience bearing a staff and appointed him Commander of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping, upon returning from his frontier tour of duty, a wound to his hand left him unable to hold the audience tablet. The emperor granted him permission to attend audience bearing a staff and appointed him commander of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 先是，范廷召、桑讚所將邊兵臨敵退衄，言者請罪之。

translations.literal: Earlier, the frontier troops led by Fan Tingzhao and Sang Zan had retreated before the enemy; critics requested that they be punished.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, the frontier troops under Fan Tingzhao and Sang Zan had retreated before the enemy, and critics at court called for their punishment.

sentences.zh: 以問瓊，瓊對曰：「兵違將令，於法當誅。

translations.literal: The emperor asked Qiong, and Qiong replied: "When troops disobey their commander's orders, by law they should be executed."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked Qiong for his view. Qiong replied: "When troops disobey their commander's orders, the law calls for execution."

sentences.zh: 然陛下去歲已釋其罪，今復行之，又方屯諸路，非時代易，臣恐眾心疑懼。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty already pardoned their crime last year; to punish them again now, when troops are garrisoned on many routes and it is not the season for rotation, I fear the men will become suspicious and fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty already pardoned them last year. To punish them again now, while troops are garrisoned across many routes and it is not the season for rotation, would, I fear, sow suspicion and alarm among the ranks.

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The punishment was then halted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 景德中，車駕北巡。

translations.literal: During the Jingde era, the imperial carriage toured north.
translations.idiomatic: During the Jingde era the emperor personally led a northern tour.

sentences.zh: 時前軍已與敵接戰，上欲親臨營壘，或勸南還，瓊曰：「敵師已老，陛下宜親往，以督其成。

translations.literal: At the time the vanguard had already joined battle with the enemy; the emperor wished to visit the camps in person. Some advised returning south. Qiong said: "The enemy army is already weary; Your Majesty should go in person to oversee their defeat."
translations.idiomatic: The vanguard had already engaged the enemy, and the emperor wished to visit the camps in person. Some advisers urged him to return south. Qiong said: "The enemy army is already exhausted. Your Majesty should go in person to ensure victory."

sentences.zh: 」上悅，即日進幸澶淵。

translations.literal: The emperor was pleased and that same day advanced to Chanyuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was pleased and that same day advanced to Chanyuan.

sentences.zh: 明年，以罷兵，料簡兵卒諸班直十年者出補軍校，年老者退為本班剩員。

translations.literal: The following year, upon the cessation of hostilities, a review was conducted: garrison regulars of ten years' service in the various guard units were selected for promotion to officer rank, while the aged were retired to surplus positions in their original units.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, after the truce, a review was held: guard regulars with ten years of service were selected for promotion to officer rank, while older men were retired to surplus positions within their original units.

sentences.zh: 瓊進曰：「此非激勸之道，宿衛豈不勞乎？

translations.literal: Qiong submitted: "This is not the way to encourage merit—is palace guard duty not arduous as well?"
translations.idiomatic: Qiong submitted: "This is no way to reward merit. Is palace guard duty not arduous as well?"

sentences.zh: 」自是八年者皆得敘補焉。

translations.literal: From then on, those with eight years' service were all permitted promotion.
translations.idiomatic: From then on, even those with eight years of service were eligible for promotion.

sentences.zh: 馬軍都校葛霸權步軍司，會以疾在告，令瓊兼領二司。

translations.literal: Ge Ba, colonel of the Cavalry Guard, was acting head of the Infantry Bureau; when he fell ill and took leave, Qiong was ordered to concurrently command both bureaus.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ba, colonel of the Cavalry Guard, was acting head of the Infantry Bureau. When he fell ill and took leave, Qiong was ordered to command both bureaus concurrently.

sentences.zh: 瓊從容上言曰：「臣衰老，儻又有犬馬之疾，則須一將總此二職。

translations.literal: Qiong calmly submitted: "I am aged and infirm; should I again suffer some illness of old age, one general will be needed to command both these posts."
translations.idiomatic: Qiong calmly submitted: "I am old and failing. Should I again fall ill, a single general will be needed to command both posts."

sentences.zh: 臣事先朝時，侍衛都虞候以上常至十員，職位相亞，易於遷改，且使軍伍熟其名望，邊藩緩急，亦可選用。

translations.literal: When I served the previous court, there were often as many as ten Vice Commanders of the Palace Guard and above; their ranks were nearly equal, making transfer easy, and the ranks would become familiar with their reputations—so that in frontier emergencies they could also be selected for use.
translations.idiomatic: When I served the previous court, there were often as many as ten vice commanders of the Palace Guard and above. Their ranks were nearly equal, which made rotation easy and allowed the ranks to become familiar with their reputations, so that in frontier emergencies they could readily be selected for duty.

sentences.zh: 」上深然之。

translations.literal: The emperor deeply approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以久疾求解兵柄，授檢校太尉、忠武軍節度。

translations.literal: Before long, citing prolonged illness, he requested release from military command and was granted the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and the post of Military Governor of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, citing prolonged illness, he requested release from military command and was granted the honorary title of Grand Preceptor and appointed military governor of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 三年冬，疾甚，上欲親臨問之，宰相不可，乃止。

translations.literal: In the winter of the third year his illness grew severe; the emperor wished to visit him in person, but the chief ministers objected, and he desisted.
translations.idiomatic: In the winter of the third year his illness grew severe. The emperor wished to visit him in person, but the chief ministers objected, and he desisted.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十二，贈侍中。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-two and was posthumously granted the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-two and was posthumously granted the title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 瓊不識字，曉達軍政，然頗自任，罕與副將參議。

translations.literal: Qiong could not read, yet was thoroughly versed in military affairs; however, he was rather self-willed and rarely consulted with his deputy generals.
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was illiterate, yet thoroughly versed in military affairs. He was rather self-willed, however, and rarely consulted with his deputy commanders.

sentences.zh: 善訓諸子：繼勳、繼宣、繼忠、繼密、繼和、繼隆、繼元。

translations.literal: He was skilled in instructing his sons: Jixun, Jixuan, Jizhong, Jimi, Jihe, Jilong, and Jiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled at training his sons: Jixun, Jixuan, Jizhong, Jimi, Jihe, Jilong, and Jiyuan.

sentences.zh: 繼勳、繼宣最知名。

translations.literal: Jixun and Jixuan were the most renowned.
translations.idiomatic: Of these, Jixun and Jixuan were the most renowned.

sentences.zh: 子 繼勳

translations.literal: Son: Jixun.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jixun

sentences.zh: 繼勳，字紹先，初補右班殿直。

translations.literal: Jixun, styled Shaoxian, was initially appointed Right Guard Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun, styled Shaoxian, was initially appointed a Right Guard palace attendant.

sentences.zh: 儀狀頎偉，太宗見而異之，召問其家世，以瓊子對。

translations.literal: His bearing was tall and imposing; Taizong saw him and was struck by it, summoned and asked about his family background, and he replied that he was Qiong's son.
translations.idiomatic: Tall and imposing in bearing, he caught Taizong's eye. The emperor summoned him and asked about his family background; Jixun replied that he was Qiong's son.

sentences.zh: 擢寄班祗候，累遷內殿崇班。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Attendant of the Attendant Guard and successively rose to Senior Attendant of the Inner Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to attendant of the Attendant Guard and rose through successive appointments to senior attendant of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 咸平初，王均據益州。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xianping, Wang Jun held Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Xianping era, Wang Jun seized Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 以崇儀副使為益州兵馬都監、提舉西川諸州軍巡檢公事。

translations.literal: As Vice Commissioner of Honored Ceremonial he was made Military Supervisor of Yizhou and Commissioner for Inspection Affairs of the Various Prefectures and Armies of Western Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: As vice commissioner of Honored Ceremonial he was appointed military supervisor of Yizhou and commissioner overseeing inspection affairs for the prefectures and armies of western Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 招安使雷有終以兵五百授繼勳，守東郭二門，會賊攻彌牟砦，繼勳引兵轉鬥至嘉州，敗之，獲黃繖、金塗鎗以還。

translations.literal: The Pacification Commissioner Lei Youzhong gave Jixun five hundred troops to hold the two eastern gates; when the rebels attacked Mizhou Fort, Jixun led his troops fighting in retreat to Jiazhou, defeated them, and returned with a yellow parasol and gold-plated spears as trophies.
translations.idiomatic: Pacification Commissioner Lei Youzhong assigned Jixun five hundred troops to hold the two eastern gates. When the rebels attacked Mizhou Fort, Jixun led his men fighting in retreat all the way to Jiazhou, defeated them, and returned with a yellow parasol and gold-plated spears as trophies.

sentences.zh: 有終益以勁兵復進攻二門，克之，乃建幟城上。

translations.literal: Youzhong added elite troops and again attacked the two gates, captured them, and then raised banners atop the wall.
translations.idiomatic: Youzhong reinforced him with crack troops and again assaulted the two gates. Once they were taken, banners were raised atop the wall.

sentences.zh: 諸將知城拔，有終乃引軍薄天長門，賊復來拒戰。

translations.literal: When the generals knew the city had been taken, Youzhong then led his army to press against the Tianchang Gate; the rebels again came out to resist.
translations.idiomatic: When the other generals learned the city had fallen, Youzhong led his army to press against the Tianchang Gate, and the rebels came out to fight again.

sentences.zh: 會日暮，有終欲少休，繼勳曰：「賊窘矣，急擊之，無失也。

translations.literal: As dusk fell, Youzhong wished to rest briefly; Jixun said: "The rebels are cornered—strike them hard at once, and do not let the chance slip."
translations.idiomatic: As dusk fell, Youzhong wished to pause and rest. Jixun said: "The rebels are cornered. Press the attack at once—do not let the opportunity slip."

sentences.zh: 」率十數騎鏖戰，身被數創，血濡甲；

translations.literal: He led a dozen or so horsemen into fierce battle, suffered several wounds, and blood soaked his armor;
translations.idiomatic: He led a dozen or so horsemen into fierce combat, suffering several wounds until blood soaked his armor;

sentences.zh: 馬死，更馬以進。

translations.literal: his horse died, and he changed horses and pressed forward.
translations.idiomatic: when his horse was killed he mounted another and pressed forward.

sentences.zh: 會入內都知秦翰來援，賊退保子城，不敢出。

translations.literal: Just then Qin Han, Director of the Inner Palace, came to reinforce; the rebels retreated to hold the inner citadel and dared not come out.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Qin Han, director of the Inner Palace, arrived with reinforcements. The rebels retreated to the inner citadel and dared not emerge.

sentences.zh: 繼勳潛知賊欲夜遁，開圍使得潰去，均卒敗滅。

translations.literal: Jixun secretly learned the rebels intended to flee by night; he opened the encirclement and allowed them to break out and scatter, and Jun was ultimately defeated and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun secretly learned the rebels planned to flee by night. He opened the encirclement and let them break out and scatter, and Wang Jun was ultimately defeated and destroyed.

sentences.zh: 以功遷崇儀使。

translations.literal: For his merit he was promoted to Commissioner of Honored Ceremonial.
translations.idiomatic: For his achievements he was promoted to commissioner of Honored Ceremonial.

sentences.zh: 賊餘黨保山藪中，時出剽劫，乃徙綿漢劍門路都巡檢使。

translations.literal: Rebel remnants held out in mountain fastnesses and periodically emerged to plunder; he was then transferred to be Overall Inspector of the Mian-Han-Jianmen Route.
translations.idiomatic: Rebel remnants held out in mountain fastnesses and periodically emerged to plunder and raid. He was then transferred to serve as overall inspector of the Mian-Han-Jianmen route.

sentences.zh: 繼勳募惡少年偵賊動靜，窮躡岩穴，掩其不備，悉擒殺之。

translations.literal: Jixun recruited unruly youths to spy on rebel movements, tracked them relentlessly to their cliff caves, struck when they were unprepared, and captured and killed them all.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun recruited tough young men to spy on rebel movements, tracked them relentlessly to their mountain caves, struck when they were unprepared, and captured and killed them all.

sentences.zh: 又徙峽路鈐轄，還朝，遷洛苑使、幷代州鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to Controller of the Gorges Route; upon returning to court he was promoted to Director of the Luoyang Park and Controller of Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: He was next transferred to controller of the Gorges route. Upon returning to court he was promoted to director of the Luoyang Park and controller of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 徙屯岢嵐軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to garrison at Kelan Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to garrison Kelan Army.

sentences.zh: 契丹聚兵五萬屯草城川，繼勳登高望之，謂軍使賈宗曰：「彼眾而陣不整，將不才也。

translations.literal: The Khitan massed fifty thousand troops at Caochengchuan; Jixun climbed high to observe them and said to Army Commissioner Jia Zong: "They are numerous but their formation is disorderly—their commander lacks ability."
translations.idiomatic: The Khitan massed fifty thousand troops at Caochengchuan. Jixun climbed to a high vantage and observed them, then said to Army Commissioner Jia Zong: "They are numerous but their formation is disorderly—their commander lacks ability."

sentences.zh: 我兵雖少，可以奇取勝。

translations.literal: Though our troops are few, we can win by a surprise stroke.
translations.idiomatic: Though our force is small, we can win by a surprise attack.

sentences.zh: 先伏兵山下，敵見我弱，必急攻我。

translations.literal: First hide troops below the hill; when the enemy sees we are weak, they will surely attack us urgently.
translations.idiomatic: First conceal troops below the hill. When the enemy sees how weak we appear, they will surely press the attack.

sentences.zh: 我誘之南走，爾起乘之，當大潰。

translations.literal: I will lure them south in flight; you rise and strike them, and they should collapse in great disorder.
translations.idiomatic: I will lure them into a feigned retreat to the south. You rise and strike from ambush, and they should collapse utterly.

sentences.zh: 」轉戰至寒光嶺，伏發，契丹果敗，相蹂躪死者萬餘人，獲馬、牛、橐駝甚眾。

translations.literal: Fighting in retreat to Hanguang Ridge, the ambush was sprung; the Khitan were indeed defeated, trampling one another to death in numbers exceeding ten thousand, and a great many horses, cattle, and camels were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Fighting in feigned retreat to Hanguang Ridge, the ambush was sprung. The Khitan were routed; more than ten thousand were trampled to death in the chaos, and a great many horses, cattle, and camels were captured.

sentences.zh: 遷弓箭庫使，賜金帶、錦袍，領榮州刺史，徙麟、府州鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Bow and Arrow Storehouse, granted a gold belt and brocade robe, given concurrent charge as Prefect of Rongzhou, and transferred to Controller of Lin and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Bow and Arrow Storehouse, granted a gold belt and brocade robe, given concurrent charge as prefect of Rongzhou, and transferred to controller of Lin and Fu.

sentences.zh: 時屯兵河外，饋運不屬。

translations.literal: At the time troops were garrisoned beyond the river, and supply transport could not keep up.
translations.idiomatic: Troops were then garrisoned beyond the river, and supply lines could not keep pace.

sentences.zh: 繼勳扼兔毛川，援送軍食，師乃濟。

translations.literal: Jixun held Tumaochuan, escorted and delivered army provisions, and the army was thus able to cross.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun held Tumaochuan, escorted grain supplies to the army, and the troops were thus able to cross.

sentences.zh: 徙知環州，又徙瀛州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to serve as Prefect of Huanzhou, and again transferred to serve as Administrator of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Huanzhou, and later transferred again to serve as administrator of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 時歲饑，募富人出粟以給貧者。

translations.literal: At the time there was famine; he recruited the wealthy to contribute grain to supply the poor.
translations.idiomatic: Famine struck the region, and he recruited wealthy households to contribute grain for the poor.

sentences.zh: 明年大稔，木生連理者四，郡人上治狀請留。

translations.literal: The next year there was a great harvest; four trees grew with conjoined trunks; the people of the prefecture submitted a report on good governance requesting he be retained.
translations.idiomatic: The next year brought a bountiful harvest, and four trees were found growing with conjoined trunks. The people of the prefecture submitted a report on his governance requesting that he be retained.

sentences.zh: 遷內藏庫使，以宮苑使奉使契丹。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of the Inner Treasury and sent as Palace Park Commissioner on an embassy to the Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to director of the Inner Treasury and dispatched to the Khitan as palace park commissioner on an embassy.

sentences.zh: 還，知定州，遷西上閤門使、昭州團練使，徙鄜延路鈐轄，坐市馬虧價失官。

translations.literal: Upon returning he served as Prefect of Dingzhou, was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and Military Commissioner of Zhaozhou, was transferred to Controller of the Fuyan Route, and lost his post for purchasing horses at a loss.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning he served as prefect of Dingzhou, was promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner and military commissioner of Zhaozhou, then transferred to controller of the Fuyan route. He lost his post for having purchased horses at a loss.

sentences.zh: 已而復為西上閤門使、榮州刺史、知冀州、領果州團練使。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Western Upper Gate Commissioner, Prefect of Rongzhou, Administrator of Jizhou, and concurrently Military Commissioner of Guozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was restored as Western Upper Gate Commissioner, prefect of Rongzhou, administrator of Jizhou, and concurrently military commissioner of Guozhou.

sentences.zh: 徙貝州，復知瀛州。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Beizhou and again served as Administrator of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Beizhou and again served as administrator of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭謝禮成，徙昭信軍節度使，為莊獻明肅太后山陵、莊懿太后園陵都總管，以老病乞骸骨。

translations.literal: When the Thanksgiving ceremony was completed, he was transferred to Military Governor of the Zhaoxin Army, appointed Overall Director of the tomb of Empress Dowager Zhuangxian Mingsu and the garden tomb of Empress Dowager Zhuangyi, and requested retirement on grounds of age and illness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Thanksgiving ceremony was completed, he was transferred to military governor of the Zhaoxin Army and appointed overall director of the tombs of Empress Dowager Zhuangxian Mingsu and Empress Dowager Zhuangyi. He then requested retirement on grounds of age and illness.

sentences.zh: 召見便殿，許一子扶掖，俾勿拜，聽辭管軍。

translations.literal: He was summoned to audience in the side hall; permission was granted for one son to support him; he was excused from bowing and allowed to resign his military command.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to audience in the side hall. The emperor permitted one son to support him, excused him from bowing, and allowed him to resign his military command.

sentences.zh: 授建雄軍節度使、知滑州。

translations.literal: He was appointed Military Governor of the Jianxiong Army and Administrator of Huazhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed military governor of the Jianxiong Army and administrator of Huazhou.

sentences.zh: 河水暴溢，齧堤岸，繼勳雖老，躬自督役，露坐河上，暮夜猶不輟，水乃殺怒，滑人德之。

translations.literal: The river waters surged and overflowed, gnawing at the dikes; though Jixun was old, he personally supervised the labor, sitting in the open on the riverbank without ceasing day or night; the waters then abated, and the people of Huazhou were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: The river surged and overflowed, eroding the dikes. Though Jixun was old, he personally supervised the repair work, sitting in the open on the riverbank without rest day or night. The flood eventually subsided, and the people of Huazhou were deeply grateful.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八，輟視朝一日，贈太尉。

translations.literal: He died at the age of seventy-eight; court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of seventy-eight. Court audiences were suspended for one day, and he was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 繼勳性謙，有機略，善撫禦士卒，臨戰輒勝。

translations.literal: Jixun was modest in nature, possessed strategic cunning, was skilled at comforting and controlling troops, and whenever he fought invariably won.
translations.idiomatic: Jixun was modest by nature, possessed strategic cunning, excelled at winning the loyalty of his troops, and invariably prevailed in battle.

sentences.zh: 在蜀有威名，號「神將」。

translations.literal: In Shu he had a formidable reputation and was called the "Divine General."
translations.idiomatic: In Sichuan he enjoyed a formidable reputation and was known as the "Divine General."

sentences.zh: 子 繼宣

translations.literal: Son: Jixuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jixuan

sentences.zh: 繼宣，字舜舉。

translations.literal: Jixuan, styled Shunju.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan, styled Shunju,

sentences.zh: 幼善騎射，頗工筆劄，知讀書。

translations.literal: From youth he was skilled in horsemanship and archery, quite adept at writing, and knew how to read.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he excelled at horsemanship and archery, was accomplished at writing, and had a solid literary education.

sentences.zh: 以恩補西頭供奉官、惠民河巡督漕船。

translations.literal: By privilege of birth he was appointed Western Attendant and overseer of grain-transport ships on the Huimin Canal.
translations.idiomatic: By privilege of birth he was appointed a Western Attendant and assigned to oversee grain-transport ships on the Huimin Canal.

sentences.zh: 會歲饑多盜，兼沿河巡檢捉賊，遷閤門祗候、邠州兵馬都監。

translations.literal: When famine brought many bandits, he additionally served as river-route inspector to capture thieves; he was promoted to Gate Attendant and Military Supervisor of Binzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When famine brought a surge of banditry, he was also assigned as river-route inspector to hunt down thieves. He was promoted to Gate Attendant and military supervisor of Binzhou.

sentences.zh: 曹瑋守邠，數與言兵，薦其可用。

translations.literal: Cao Wei garrisoned Bin; he often discussed military affairs with Jixuan and recommended him as capable.
translations.idiomatic: Cao Wei was then garrisoning Binzhou. He often discussed military affairs with Jixuan and recommended him as a capable officer.

sentences.zh: 乾興初，以內殿崇班為益州都監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianxing, as Senior Attendant of the Inner Palace he was made Overall Supervisor of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qianxing era he was appointed overall supervisor of Yizhou with the rank of senior attendant of the Inner Palace.

sentences.zh: 蜀人富侈，元夕大張燈，知府薛奎戒以備盜，繼宣籍惡少年飲犒之，使夜中潛誌盜背，明日皆獲。

translations.literal: The people of Shu were wealthy and extravagant; on the Lantern Festival they displayed many lanterns. Prefect Xue Kui warned them to guard against thieves. Jixuan registered unruly youths, treated them to food and drink, and had them secretly mark the backs of thieves at night; the next day all were captured.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Shu were wealthy and extravagant, and on the Lantern Festival they displayed elaborate lantern displays. Prefect Xue Kui warned them to guard against thieves. Jixuan registered unruly youths, treated them to food and drink, and had them secretly mark the backs of thieves in the night. The next day all were captured.

sentences.zh: 歷磁、相、邢、洺都巡檢使，知安肅軍，徙保州。

translations.literal: He served successively as Overall Inspector of Ci, Xiang, Xing, and Ming; Administrator of Ansu Army; and was transferred to Baozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served successively as overall inspector of Ci, Xiang, Xing, and Ming, as administrator of Ansu Army, and was then transferred to Baozhou.

sentences.zh: 累遷禮賓使、益州路兵馬鈐轄。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Commissioner of Ceremonial Reception and Controller of Troops on the Yizhou Route.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to commissioner of Ceremonial Reception and controller of troops on the Yizhou route.

sentences.zh: 還，為西上閤門使、涇原路鈐轄兼安撫使、知渭州，遷四方館使、昭州刺史、知雄州。

translations.literal: Upon returning to court he became Western Upper Gate Commissioner, Controller and Pacification Commissioner of the Jingyuan Route and Administrator of Weizhou; he was promoted to Commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, Prefect of Zhaozhou, and Administrator of Xiongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Upon returning to court he was appointed Western Upper Gate Commissioner, controller and pacification commissioner of the Jingyuan route, and administrator of Weizhou. He was later promoted to commissioner of the Four Directions Hall, prefect of Zhaozhou, and administrator of Xiongzhou.

sentences.zh: 初，元昊反，聲言侵關隴。

translations.literal: Initially, when Yuanhao rebelled, he declared he would invade Guan and Long.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanhao first rebelled, he declared his intention to invade the Guan and Long region.

sentences.zh: 繼宣請備麟府。

translations.literal: Jixuan requested preparations at Lin and Fu.
translations.idiomatic: Jixuan petitioned for defensive preparations at Lin and Fu.

sentences.zh: 未幾，羌兵果入寇河外，陷豐州。

translations.literal: Before long, Qiang troops indeed invaded beyond the river and captured Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Qiang forces did invade beyond the river and captured Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 擢捧日天武四廂都指揮使、恩州團練使、知幷州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Bearing Celestial Martial Guard, Military Commissioner of Enzhou, and Administrator of Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Bearing Celestial Martial Guard, military commissioner of Enzhou, and administrator of Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 俄寇麟府，繼宣帥兵營陵井，抵天門關。

translations.literal: Soon the enemy raided Lin and Fu; Jixuan led troops to encamp at Lingjing and reached Tianmen Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the enemy raided Lin and Fu. Jixuan led his troops to encamp at Lingjing and advanced to Tianmen Pass.

sentences.zh: 是夕大雨，及河，師半濟，黑凌暴合，舟不得進，乃具牲酒為文以禱。

translations.literal: That evening there was heavy rain; when they reached the river, the army was half across when black ice suddenly closed together and boats could not advance; he then prepared sacrificial offerings and wine and wrote a prayer text to supplicate.
translations.idiomatic: That evening a heavy rain fell. When they reached the river the army was half across when black ice suddenly closed over the water and the boats could not advance. Jixuan then prepared sacrificial offerings and wine and wrote a prayer to supplicate the spirits.

sentences.zh: 已而凌解，師濟，進屯府谷，間遣勇士夜亂賊營。

translations.literal: Before long the ice broke up, the army crossed, advanced to garrison at Fugu, and intermittently sent brave men to raid the enemy camp by night.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the ice broke up and the army crossed. They advanced to garrison at Fugu and intermittently sent brave men to raid the enemy camp by night.

sentences.zh: 又募黥配廂軍，得二千餘人，號清邊軍，命偏將王凱主之。

translations.literal: He also recruited tattooed convicts assigned to garrison troops, obtaining more than two thousand men; they were called the Clear-the-Border Army, and he ordered Deputy General Wang Kai to command them.
translations.idiomatic: He also recruited tattooed convicts assigned to garrison duty, assembling more than two thousand men. They were called the Clear-the-Border Army, and he placed them under the command of Deputy General Wang Kai.

sentences.zh: 軍次三松嶺，賊數萬眾圍之，清邊軍奮起，斬首千餘級。

translations.literal: The army halted at Sansong Ridge; tens of thousands of rebels surrounded them; the Clear-the-Border Army rose up fiercely and cut off more than a thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: At Sansong Ridge the army was surrounded by tens of thousands of rebels. The Clear-the-Border Army fought back fiercely and cut off more than a thousand enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 其相躪藉死者不可勝計。

translations.literal: Those trampled to death among them were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: The number trampled to death in the chaos was beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 築寧遠砦，相視地脈，鑿石出泉。

translations.literal: He built Ningyuan Fort, surveyed the terrain's water veins, and drilled through rock to bring forth a spring.
translations.idiomatic: He built Ningyuan Fort, surveyed the terrain for water sources, and drilled through rock to bring forth a spring.

sentences.zh: 已而城五砦，遷眉州防禦使，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he fortified five forts, was transferred to Defense Commissioner of Meizhou, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he fortified five additional forts, was transferred to defense commissioner of Meizhou, and died.

sentences.zh: 范廷召

translations.literal: Fan Tingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tingzhao

sentences.zh: 宋初，從平李筠、李重進，轉本班都知。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Song, he followed in the pacification of Li Yun and Li Chongjin and was transferred to Director of his Guard Unit.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Song he took part in the suppression of Li Yun and Li Chongjin and was promoted to director of his guard unit.

sentences.zh: 又從征太原，再轉散都頭、都虞候、領費州刺史。

translations.literal: He again followed the campaign against Taiyuan and was successively transferred to Loose Company Commander, Vice Commander, and concurrently Prefect of Feizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He also took part in the campaign against Taiyuan and rose through successive appointments to loose company commander, vice commander, and concurrently prefect of Feizhou.

sentences.zh: 太平興國中，以日騎軍都指揮使從平太原，征范陽。

translations.literal: During Taiping Xingguo, as Commander of the Day-Cavalry Guard he followed in the pacification of Taiyuan and the campaign against Fanyang.
translations.idiomatic: During the Taiping Xingguo era, as commander of the Day-Cavalry Guard he took part in the pacification of Taiyuan and the campaign against Fanyang.

sentences.zh: 秦王廷美嘗遣親吏閻懷忠、趙瓊犒禁軍列校，廷召預焉，坐出為唐州馬步軍都指揮使。

translations.literal: Prince of Qin Tingmei once sent personal clerks Yan Huaizhong and Zhao Qiong to reward the column commanders of the Palace Guard; Tingzhao was among them and was demoted to Commander of Cavalry and Infantry at Tangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince of Qin Tingmei once sent personal clerks Yan Huaizhong and Zhao Qiong to distribute rewards among the column commanders of the Palace Guard. Tingzhao was implicated and was demoted to commander of cavalry and infantry at Tangzhou.

sentences.zh: 雍熙三年，議北征，召入為馬步軍都軍頭、領平州刺史、幽州道前軍先鋒都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yongxi, when a northern campaign was discussed, he was recalled as Commander-in-Chief of Cavalry and Infantry, concurrently Prefect of Pingzhou, and Vanguard Commander of the Youzhou Route advance force.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Yongxi, when a northern campaign was being planned, he was recalled as commander-in-chief of cavalry and infantry, concurrently prefect of Pingzhou, and vanguard commander of the Youzhou route advance force.

sentences.zh: 與賊遇固安南，破其眾三千，斬首千餘級，克固安、新城二縣，乘勝下涿州。

translations.literal: He encountered the enemy south of Gu'an, broke their force of three thousand, cut off more than a thousand heads, captured the two counties of Gu'an and Xincheng, and pressed the advantage to take Zhuozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He encountered the enemy south of Gu'an, routed a force of three thousand, cut off more than a thousand heads, captured the counties of Gu'an and Xincheng, and pressed the advantage to take Zhuozhou.

sentences.zh: 廷召復與賊戰，中流矢，血漬甲縷，神色自若，督戰益急，詔褒之。

translations.literal: Tingzhao again fought the enemy, was struck by a flying arrow, blood soaking the threads of his armor; his expression remained calm, and he pressed the battle even harder; an edict commended him.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao fought the enemy again and was struck by a flying arrow, blood soaking the threads of his armor. His expression remained calm and he pressed the battle even harder. An edict commended him for his valor.

sentences.zh: 師還，遷日騎右廂都指揮使、領本州圍練使，又遷左廂，移領高州。

translations.literal: When the army returned, he was transferred to Commander of the Right Wing of the Day-Cavalry Guard and concurrently Military Commissioner of his native prefecture; he was again transferred to the Left Wing and moved to concurrently serve as Military Commissioner of Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, he was made commander of the Right Wing of the Day-Cavalry Guard and concurrently military commissioner of his home prefecture. He was later transferred to the Left Wing and reassigned as military commissioner of Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，出為齊州防禦使，數月，授捧日天武四廂都指揮使、領澄州防禦使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong, he went out as Defense Commissioner of Qizhou; several months later he was appointed Commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Bearing Celestial Martial Guard and concurrently Defense Commissioner of Chengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era he was posted as defense commissioner of Qizhou. Several months later he was appointed commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Bearing Celestial Martial Guard and concurrently defense commissioner of Chengzhou.

sentences.zh: 二年，轉殿前都虞候、領涼州觀察使、鎮州副都部署。

translations.literal: In the second year he was transferred to Vice Commander of the Palace Guard, concurrently Observation Commissioner of Liangzhou, and Deputy Overall Commander at Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was transferred to vice commander of the Palace Guard, concurrently observation commissioner of Liangzhou, and deputy overall commander at Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 大破契丹三萬眾於徐河，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: He greatly defeated thirty thousand Khitan at Xuhe, cutting off several thousand heads.
translations.idiomatic: He routed thirty thousand Khitan at Xuhe, cutting off several thousand heads.

sentences.zh: 淳化二年，為平虜橋砦都部署，歷幷代、環慶兩路副部署。

translations.literal: In the second year of Chunhua he was made Overall Commander of Pingluqiao Fort and successively served as Deputy Commander of the Bing-Dai and Huan-Qing routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Chunhua he was appointed overall commander of Pingluqiao Fort and successively served as deputy commander of the Bing-Dai and Huan-Qing routes.

sentences.zh: 至道中，遣將從五路討李繼遷，命廷召副李繼隆為環慶靈都部署。

translations.literal: During Zhidao, generals were dispatched along five routes to campaign against Li Jiqian; Tingzhao was ordered to serve under Li Jilong as Overall Commander of Huan, Qing, and Ling.
translations.idiomatic: During the Zhidao era generals were dispatched along five routes to campaign against Li Jiqian. Tingzhao was ordered to serve under Li Jilong as overall commander of Huan, Qing, and Ling.

sentences.zh: 廷召出延州路，與賊遇白池，獲米募軍主吃囉等兵器、鎧甲數萬。

translations.literal: Tingzhao advanced by the Yanzhou route and encountered the enemy at Baichi; he captured Chiluo, leader of the rice-recruited army, and tens of thousands of weapons and suits of armor.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao advanced by the Yanzhou route and encountered the enemy at Baichi. He captured Chiluo, leader of the rice-recruited army, along with tens of thousands of weapons and suits of armor.

sentences.zh: 是役也，諸將失期，獨廷召與王超大小數十戰，屢克捷，上嘉之。

translations.literal: In this campaign the other generals missed their deadlines; only Tingzhao and Wang Chao fought several dozen engagements large and small, repeatedly winning victories, and the emperor commended them.
translations.idiomatic: In this campaign the other generals failed to meet their deadlines. Only Tingzhao and Wang Chao fought several dozen engagements, large and small, and repeatedly won victories. The emperor commended them.

sentences.zh: 俄又為幷代兩路都部署。

translations.literal: Soon he was again made Overall Commander of the Bing and Dai routes.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed overall commander of the Bing and Dai routes.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使、領河西軍節度，為定州行營都部署。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry, concurrently Military Governor of the Hexi Army, and Overall Commander of the mobile camp at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry, given the concurrent title of military governor of the Hexi Army, and appointed overall commander of the mobile camp at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 咸平二年，契丹入塞，車駕北巡。

translations.literal: In the second year of Xianping the Khitan entered the frontier passes; the imperial carriage toured north.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Xianping the Khitan invaded the frontier, and the emperor personally led a northern tour.

sentences.zh: 廷召與戰瀛州西，斬首二萬級，逐北至莫州東三十里，又斬首萬餘，奪其所掠老幼數萬口，契丹遁去。

translations.literal: Tingzhao fought them west of Yingzhou, cutting off twenty thousand heads; he pursued them north to thirty li east of Mozhou, cut off more than ten thousand more, recovered tens of thousands of old and young they had seized, and the Khitan fled.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao fought them west of Yingzhou and cut off twenty thousand heads. He pursued them north to a point thirty li east of Mozhou, cut off more than ten thousand more, recovered tens of thousands of elderly and children the Khitan had seized, and the invaders fled.

sentences.zh: 師還，錄功加檢校太傅，益賦邑，又改殿前都指揮使。

translations.literal: When the army returned, his merit was recorded and he was given the honorary title of Grand Tutor, increased fief income, and again made Commander of the Palace Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When the army returned, his achievements were recorded and he was granted the honorary title of Grand Tutor, given an increase in fief income, and appointed commander of the Palace Guard.

sentences.zh: 四年正月被疾，車駕臨問，卒，年七十五，贈侍中。

translations.literal: In the first month of the fourth year he fell ill; the imperial carriage visited to inquire after him; he died at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously granted the title of Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the fourth year he fell ill. The emperor personally visited to inquire after him. He died at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously granted the title of Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 廷召在軍四十餘年，由顯德以來，凡親征，未嘗不從。

translations.literal: Tingzhao was in the army for more than forty years; from Xiande onward, whenever the emperor personally campaigned, he never failed to follow.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao served in the army for more than forty years. From the Xiande era onward, whenever the emperor personally led a campaign, he was always in attendance.

sentences.zh: 善騎射，嘗出獵，有群鳥飛過，廷召發矢，並貫其三，觀者駭異。

translations.literal: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery; once while out hunting, a flock of birds flew past; Tingzhao loosed an arrow and pierced three of them together; onlookers were astonished.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in horsemanship and archery. Once while out hunting, a flock of birds flew past and Tingzhao loosed a single arrow that pierced three of them together. Onlookers were astonished.

sentences.zh: 性惡飛禽，所至處彈射殆絕。

translations.literal: By nature he hated flying birds; wherever he went he shot them nearly to extinction.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he detested birds, and wherever he went he shot them nearly to extinction.

sentences.zh: 尤不喜驢鳴，聞必擊殺之。

translations.literal: He especially disliked the braying of donkeys; whenever he heard it he would strike and kill them.
translations.idiomatic: He especially could not abide the braying of donkeys; whenever he heard it he would have the animal beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 子守均，至散員都虞候、演州刺史；

translations.literal: His son Shoujun rose to Vice Commander of Loose Company and Prefect of Yanzhou;
translations.idiomatic: His son Shoujun rose to vice commander of Loose Company and prefect of Yanzhou;

sentences.zh: 守信，內殿承製、閤門祗候；

translations.literal: Shouxin, Inner Palace Artisan and Gate Attendant;
translations.idiomatic: Shouxin served as inner palace artisan and gate attendant;

sentences.zh: 守宣，內殿崇班；

translations.literal: Shouxuan, Senior Attendant of the Inner Palace;
translations.idiomatic: Shouxuan served as senior attendant of the Inner Palace;

sentences.zh: 守慶更名珪，後為西京作坊副使、淮南江浙荊湖制置發運副使。

translations.literal: Shouqing changed his name to Gui and later served as Deputy Director of the Western Capital Workshop and Deputy Commissioner for Transport and Supply in Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu.
translations.idiomatic: Shouqing changed his name to Gui and later served as deputy director of the Western Capital workshop and deputy commissioner for transport and supply in Huainan, Jiang-Zhe, and Jing-Hu.

sentences.zh: 葛霸，真定人。

translations.literal: Ge Ba was a man of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ba was a native of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 姿表雄毅，善擊刺騎射。

translations.literal: His bearing was heroic and resolute; he was skilled in thrusting, riding, and shooting.
translations.idiomatic: Heroic and imposing in bearing, he was skilled in close combat, horsemanship, and archery.

sentences.zh: 始事太宗於藩邸；

translations.literal: He first served Taizong at his princely residence;
translations.idiomatic: He first entered the service of Taizong when the latter was still a prince;

sentences.zh: 踐阼，補殿前指揮使，稍遷本班都知，三遷至散員都虞候。

translations.literal: when Taizong ascended the throne, he was appointed Palace Guard Commander, gradually promoted to Director of his Guard Unit, and after three promotions reached Vice Commander of Loose Company.
translations.idiomatic: when Taizong ascended the throne he was appointed a palace guard commander, gradually rose to director of his guard unit, and after three promotions reached vice commander of Loose Company.

sentences.zh: 雍熙中，幽州之師失律，大補軍校，以霸為驍騎軍都指揮使、領檀州刺史，戍定州。

translations.literal: During Yongxi, when the Youzhou army lost discipline, military officers were greatly replenished; Ba was made Commander of the Valiant Cavalry Guard, concurrently Prefect of Tanzhou, and garrisoned at Dingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During the Yongxi era, after the Youzhou army lost discipline, military officers were greatly replenished. Ba was appointed commander of the Valiant Cavalry Guard, given concurrent charge as prefect of Tanzhou, and garrisoned at Dingzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘗遇敵唐河，與戰，敗走之，斬獲甚眾。

translations.literal: He once encountered the enemy at Tanghe, fought them, defeated and routed them, and cut down and captured a great many.
translations.idiomatic: He once encountered the enemy at Tanghe, fought them, routed their force, and cut down and captured a great many.

sentences.zh: 俄召為御前忠佐馬步軍都軍頭。

translations.literal: Soon he was recalled as Commander-in-Chief of the Imperial Front Loyal Assistant Cavalry and Infantry.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as commander-in-chief of the Imperial Front Loyal Assistant Cavalry and Infantry.

sentences.zh: 端拱初，出為博州團練使，歷潞、代二州部署。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Duangong he went out as Military Commissioner of Bozhou and successively served as Commander at Lu and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Duangong era he was posted as military commissioner of Bozhou and successively served as deployment commander at Lu and Dai.

sentences.zh: 淳化元年，擢殿前都虞候、領潘州觀察使，為高陽關副都部署，進都部署。

translations.literal: In the first year of Chunhua he was promoted to Vice Commander of the Palace Guard, concurrently Observation Commissioner of Panzhou, made Deputy Overall Commander at Gaoyang Pass, and advanced to Overall Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Chunhua he was promoted to vice commander of the Palace Guard, given the concurrent title of observation commissioner of Panzhou, appointed deputy overall commander at Gaoyang Pass, and later promoted to overall commander.

sentences.zh: 凡七戰。

translations.literal: In all he fought seven battles.
translations.idiomatic: In all he fought seven battles.

sentences.zh: 召還，制授保順軍節度，典軍如故。

translations.literal: He was recalled and appointed Military Governor of the Baoshun Army, continuing to command troops as before.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled and appointed military governor of the Baoshun Army while continuing to command troops as before.

sentences.zh: 出為鎮州都部署，徙天雄軍。

translations.literal: He went out as Overall Commander at Zhenzhou and was transferred to the Tianxiong Army.
translations.idiomatic: He was posted as overall commander at Zhenzhou and later transferred to the Tianxiong Army.

sentences.zh: 咸平三年，車駕勞師於大名，霸與石保吉同來覲。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xianping the imperial carriage rewarded the troops at Daming; Ba and Shi Baoji came together to audience.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Xianping the emperor went to Daming to reward the troops. Ba and Shi Baoji came together to audience.

sentences.zh: 時康保裔沒於河間，即日以霸為貝、冀、高陽關前軍行營都部署。

translations.literal: At the time Kang Baoyi had perished at Hejian; that same day Ba was made Overall Commander of the advance camp at Bei, Ji, and Gaoyang Pass.
translations.idiomatic: Kang Baoyi had just perished at Hejian, and that same day Ba was appointed overall commander of the advance camp at Bei, Ji, and Gaoyang Pass.

sentences.zh: 二月，就遷副都指揮使。

translations.literal: In the second month he was concurrently promoted to Vice Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month he was concurrently promoted to vice commander.

sentences.zh: 未幾，改邠寧、涇原、環慶三路都部署。

translations.literal: Before long he was reassigned as Overall Commander of the Bin-Ning, Jing-Yuan, and Huan-Qing routes.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was reassigned as overall commander of the Bin-Ning, Jing-Yuan, and Huan-Qing routes.

sentences.zh: 四年，遷侍衛馬軍都指揮使，領感德軍節度。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was transferred to Commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry and concurrently Military Governor of the Gande Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was transferred to commander of the Palace Guard Cavalry and given the concurrent title of military governor of the Gande Army.

sentences.zh: 景德元年，河決澶州橫壟埽，命為修河都部署。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jingde the Yellow River breached the Henglong Embankment at Chenzhou; he was ordered to serve as Overall Commander of River Repair.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Jingde the Yellow River breached the Henglong Embankment at Chenzhou, and he was appointed overall commander of river repair.

sentences.zh: 未行，屬北邊有警，真宗議親征，以霸為駕前西面邢洺路都部署，又副李繼隆為駕前東面排陣使，駐澶州。

translations.literal: Before he departed, alarms arose on the northern frontier; Zhenzong deliberated a personal campaign; Ba was made Overall Commander of the Xing-Ming Route on the western flank before the imperial carriage, and additionally served under Li Jilong as Battle Formation Commissioner on the eastern flank before the carriage, garrisoned at Chenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could depart, alarms arose on the northern frontier and Zhenzong deliberated a personal campaign. Ba was appointed overall commander of the Xing-Ming route on the western flank before the imperial carriage and additionally served under Li Jilong as battle formation commissioner on the eastern flank, garrisoned at Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 明年召還，以功特加封邑。

translations.literal: The following year he was recalled and specially granted increased fief on account of his merit.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was recalled and specially granted an increase in fief income for his achievements.

sentences.zh: 上言朝廷居明德心喪，尚遏音樂，請停迎授之制，奏可。

translations.literal: He submitted that the court was in the heart-mourning period for Mingde and still restrained music; he requested suspension of the welcoming and investiture ceremony, and the memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted that the court was still in the heart-mourning period for Empress Mingde and had restrained musical performances. He requested that the welcoming and investiture ceremony be suspended, and the memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以霸久典兵，年且老，罷軍職，授昭德軍節度、幷代都部署。

translations.literal: That winter, because Ba had long commanded troops and was growing old, his military post was removed; he was granted the post of Military Governor of the Zhaode Army and Overall Commander of Bing and Dai.
translations.idiomatic: That winter, because Ba had long held military command and was growing old, his military post was removed. He was appointed military governor of the Zhaode Army and overall commander of Bing and Dai.

sentences.zh: 時廷臣有隸麾下者，頗擾軍民，霸昏耄，為所罔，真宗知之，故有是召。

translations.literal: At the time there were court officials under his command who greatly harassed soldiers and civilians; Ba, senile, was deceived by them; Zhenzong knew of this, and therefore issued this recall.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there were court officials under his command who greatly harassed soldiers and civilians. Ba, growing senile, was deceived by them. Zhenzong knew of this, and therefore issued the recall.

sentences.zh: 四年夏，徙知耀州。

translations.literal: In the summer of the fourth year he was transferred to serve as Administrator of Yaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the summer of the fourth year he was transferred to serve as administrator of Yaozhou.

sentences.zh: 霸雖懦，然能謹直自持。

translations.literal: Though Ba was timid, he was able to maintain himself with scrupulous integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Though Ba was timid by nature, he maintained himself with scrupulous integrity.

sentences.zh: 會東封，表求扈蹕。

translations.literal: When the eastern feng ceremony was held, he submitted a memorial requesting to escort the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: When the eastern feng ceremony was held, he submitted a memorial requesting to escort the imperial procession.

sentences.zh: 既以疾不能從，車駕還次衛南，疾少間，迎謁行在。

translations.literal: Since illness prevented him from following, when the imperial carriage returned and halted at Weinan, his illness having eased somewhat, he came to greet and attend audience at the temporary palace.
translations.idiomatic: Illness prevented him from joining the procession. When the imperial carriage returned and halted at Weinan, his illness having eased somewhat, he came to greet the emperor at the temporary palace.

sentences.zh: 上嘉其意，勞問久之。

translations.literal: The emperor commended his intent and questioned and consoled him at length.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended his devotion and questioned and consoled him at length.

sentences.zh: 未幾卒，年七十五，贈太尉。

translations.literal: Before long he died at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he died at the age of seventy-five and was posthumously granted the title of Grand Preceptor.

sentences.zh: 子懷信、懷正、懷敏、懷煦。

translations.literal: His sons were Huaixin, Huaizheng, Huaimin, and Huaixu.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Huaixin, Huaizheng, Huaimin, and Huaixu.

sentences.zh: 懷信至如京副使；

translations.literal: Huaixin rose to Deputy Commissioner to the Capital;
translations.idiomatic: Huaixin rose to deputy commissioner to the capital;

sentences.zh: 懷煦，內殿承制；

translations.literal: Huaixu, Inner Palace Artisan;
translations.idiomatic: Huaixu served as inner palace artisan;

sentences.zh: 懷正，博州團練使、知滄、莫二州。

translations.literal: Huaizheng, Military Commissioner of Bozhou and Administrator of Cang and Mo.
translations.idiomatic: Huaizheng served as military commissioner of Bozhou and administrator of Cang and Mo.

translations.literal: 〈Son〉
translations.idiomatic: His son

sentences.zh: 懷敏

translations.literal: Huaimin.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin

sentences.zh: 懷敏以蔭授西頭供奉官，加閤門祗候。

translations.literal: Huaimin by privilege of birth was appointed Western Attendant and additionally made Gate Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin by privilege of birth was appointed a Western Attendant and additionally made a gate attendant.

sentences.zh: 歷同提點益州路刑獄、襄鄧都巡檢。

translations.literal: He successively served as Co-Commissioner for Criminal Affairs on the Yizhou Route and Overall Inspector of Xiang and Deng.
translations.idiomatic: He successively served as co-commissioner for criminal affairs on the Yizhou route and overall inspector of Xiang and Deng.

sentences.zh: 使契丹，知隰、莫、保三州，累遷東染院使、康州刺史、知雄州，就遷西上閤門使。

translations.literal: He served as envoy to the Khitan, Administrator of Xi, Mo, and Bao, was successively promoted to Director of the Eastern Dyeing Bureau, Prefect of Kangzhou, and Administrator of Xiongzhou, and was concurrently promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: He served as envoy to the Khitan and as administrator of Xi, Mo, and Bao. He rose through successive appointments to director of the Eastern Dyeing Bureau, prefect of Kangzhou, and administrator of Xiongzhou, and was concurrently promoted to Western Upper Gate Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 上《平燕策》。

translations.literal: He submitted a "Strategy for Pacifying Yan."
translations.idiomatic: He submitted a memorial titled "Strategy for Pacifying Yan."

sentences.zh: 會歲旱，塘水涸，懷敏慮契丹使至測知其廣深，乃擁界河水注之，塘復如故。

translations.literal: When drought caused the moat water to dry up, Huaimin feared that when Khitan envoys arrived they would measure its width and depth; he therefore diverted boundary river water to fill it, and the moat was restored as before.
translations.idiomatic: When drought caused the moat to dry up, Huaimin feared that Khitan envoys would measure its width and depth on arrival. He therefore diverted boundary river water to refill it, and the moat was restored to its former state.

sentences.zh: 召對邊事，復還雄州，改萊州團練使。

translations.literal: He was summoned to discuss frontier affairs, returned again to Xiongzhou, and was reassigned as Military Commissioner of Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to discuss frontier affairs, returned again to Xiongzhou, and was reassigned as military commissioner of Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 濁流砦兵叛，殺官吏潰去，懷敏發兵掩襲，盡誅其黨。

translations.literal: Troops at Zhuoliu Fort rebelled, killed officials, and fled in disorder; Huaimin dispatched troops in a surprise attack and executed all the ringleaders.
translations.idiomatic: Troops at Zhuoliu Fort rebelled, killed their officers, and fled in disorder. Huaimin dispatched troops in a surprise attack and executed all the ringleaders.

sentences.zh: 在雄州五年，徙滄州。

translations.literal: After five years at Xiongzhou he was transferred to Cangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: After five years at Xiongzhou he was transferred to Cangzhou.

sentences.zh: 懷敏為王德用妹婿，德用貶，亦絳知滁州。

translations.literal: Huaimin was the son-in-law of Wang Deyong's younger sister; when Deyong was demoted, Huaimin was also reduced in rank to Administrator of Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin was the son-in-law of Wang Deyong's younger sister. When Deyong was demoted, Huaimin was also reduced in rank and appointed administrator of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 陝西用兵，起為涇原路馬步軍副總管兼涇原秦鳳兩路經略、安撫副使。

translations.literal: When warfare broke out in Shaanxi, he was recalled as Deputy Overall Commander of Cavalry and Infantry on the Jingyuan Route and concurrently Deputy Commissioner for Frontier Strategy and Pacification on the Jingyuan and Qin-Feng routes.
translations.idiomatic: When warfare broke out in Shaanxi, he was recalled as deputy overall commander of cavalry and infantry on the Jingyuan route and concurrently deputy commissioner for frontier strategy and pacification on the Jingyuan and Qin-Feng routes.

sentences.zh: 既入對，以曹瑋嘗所被介胄賜之，令制置鄜延、環慶兩路存廢砦柵。

translations.literal: After entering for audience, he was granted the armor Cao Wei had once worn and ordered to arrange which forts and stockades on the Fuyan and Huan-Qing routes should be retained or abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: After his audience with the emperor, he was granted the armor Cao Wei had once worn and ordered to determine which forts and stockades on the Fuyan and Huan-Qing routes should be retained or abandoned.

sentences.zh: 擢龍神衛四廂都指揮、眉州防禦使、本路副都總管、知涇原。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, Defense Commissioner of Meizhou, Deputy Overall Commander of his route, and Administrator of Jingyuan.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to commander of the Four Wings of the Dragon Spirit Guard, defense commissioner of Meizhou, deputy overall commander of his route, and administrator of Jingyuan.

sentences.zh: 遷捧日天武四廂都指揮使、鄜延路副都總管。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Bearing Celestial Martial Guard and Deputy Overall Commander of the Fuyan Route.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to commander of the Four Wings of the Sun-Bearing Celestial Martial Guard and deputy overall commander of the Fuyan route.

sentences.zh: 進殿前都虞候、知延州。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Vice Commander of the Palace Guard and Administrator of Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice commander of the Palace Guard and administrator of Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 范仲淹言其猾懦不知兵，復徙涇原路兼招討、經略、安撫副使。

translations.literal: Fan Zhongyan said he was cunning and timid and ignorant of military affairs; he was again transferred to the Jingyuan Route as concurrently Deputy Pacification, Frontier Strategy, and Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Fan Zhongyan declared him cunning, timid, and ignorant of military affairs. He was reassigned to the Jingyuan route as concurrently deputy pacification, frontier strategy, and pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 慶曆二年，元昊寇鎮戎軍，懷敏出瓦亭砦，督砦主都監許思純、環慶路都監劉賀、天聖砦主張貴，及緣邊都巡檢使向進、劉湛、趙瑜等禦敵。

translations.literal: In the second year of Qingli, Yuanhao raided Zhenrong Army; Huaimin advanced from Wating Fort, directing Fort Commander and Supervisor Xu Sichun, Huan-Qing Route Supervisor Liu He, Tiansheng Fort Commander Zhang Gui, and frontier Overall Inspectors Xiang Jin, Liu Zhan, Zhao Yu, and others to resist the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Qingli, Yuanhao raided Zhenrong Army. Huaimin advanced from Wating Fort and directed Fort Commander and Supervisor Xu Sichun, Huan-Qing route supervisor Liu He, Tiansheng Fort Commander Zhang Gui, and frontier overall inspectors Xiang Jin, Liu Zhan, Zhao Yu, and others to resist the enemy.

sentences.zh: 軍次安邊砦，給芻秣未絕，懷敏輒離軍，夜至開遠堡北一里而舍。

translations.literal: The army halted at Anbian Fort; fodder was still being distributed when Huaimin abruptly left the army and by night encamped one li north of Kaiyuan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: The army halted at Anbian Fort. Fodder was still being distributed when Huaimin abruptly left the army and by night encamped one li north of Kaiyuan Fort.

sentences.zh: 既而自鎮戎軍西南，又先引從騎百餘以前，承受趙正曰：「敵近，不可輕進。

translations.literal: Then from the southwest of Zhenrong Army he again led more than a hundred mounted followers ahead; Attendant Zhao Zheng said: "The enemy is near; do not advance lightly."
translations.idiomatic: Then from the southwest of Zhenrong Army he again led more than a hundred mounted followers ahead. Attendant Zhao Zheng said: "The enemy is near. Do not advance lightly."

sentences.zh: 」懷敏乃少止。

translations.literal: Huaimin then halted briefly.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin then halted briefly.

sentences.zh: 日暮趨養馬城，與知鎮戎軍曹英及涇原路都監李知和王保王文、鎮戎軍都監李嶽、西路都巡檢使趙璘等會兵。

translations.literal: At dusk he hurried to Yangma City and joined forces with Zhenrong Army Administrator Cao Ying, Jingyuan Route Supervisors Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, and Wang Wen, Zhenrong Army Supervisor Li Yue, and Western Route Overall Inspector Zhao Lin and others.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he hurried to Yangma City and joined forces with Zhenrong Army administrator Cao Ying, Jingyuan route supervisors Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, and Wang Wen, Zhenrong Army supervisor Li Yue, and Western Route overall inspector Zhao Lin and others.

sentences.zh: 聞元昊徙軍新壕外，懷敏議質明襲之，乃命諸命將分四路趣定川砦：劉湛、向進出西水口，涇原路都監趙珣出蓮華堡，曹英、李知和出劉璠堡，懷敏出定西堡。

translations.literal: Hearing that Yuanhao had moved his army outside the new moat, Huaimin proposed a dawn attack; he then ordered the various commanders to advance by four routes toward Dingchuan Fort: Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin by the Western Water Pass, Jingyuan Route Supervisor Zhao Xun from Lianhua Fort, Cao Ying and Li Zhihe from Liu Fan Fort, and Huaimin from Dingxi Fort.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Yuanhao had moved his army outside the new moat, Huaimin proposed a dawn attack. He ordered his commanders to advance by four routes toward Dingchuan Fort: Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin by the Western Water Pass, Jingyuan route supervisor Zhao Xun from Lianhua Fort, Cao Ying and Li Zhihe from Liu Fan Fort, and Huaimin himself from Dingxi Fort.

sentences.zh: 知和與英督軍夜發。

translations.literal: Zhihe and Ying led the army out by night.
translations.idiomatic: Zhihe and Ying led their troops out by night.

sentences.zh: 翌日，湛、進行次趙福堡，遇敵，戰不勝，保向家峽，懷敏使珣、英並鎮戎軍西路巡檢李良臣、孟淵援之。

translations.literal: The next day, Zhan and Jin halted at Zhaofu Fort, encountered the enemy, fought without victory, and held at Xiangjia Gorge; Huaimin sent Zhao Xun, Ying, and Zhenrong Army Western Route Inspectors Li Liangchen and Meng Yuan to reinforce them.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Zhan and Jin halted at Zhaofu Fort, encountered the enemy, and fought without success. They fell back to hold Xiangjia Gorge. Huaimin sent Zhao Xun, Ying, and Zhenrong Army Western Route inspectors Li Liangchen and Meng Yuan to reinforce them.

sentences.zh: 俄報敵已拔柵逾邊壕，懷敏入保定川砦，敵毀板橋，斷其歸路，別為二十四道以過軍，環圍之。

translations.literal: Soon word came that the enemy had pulled up palisades and crossed the frontier moat; Huaimin entered Baodingchuan Fort; the enemy destroyed the plank bridge, cut off his retreat, made twenty-four separate crossings to pass their army through, and surrounded him.
translations.idiomatic: Soon word came that the enemy had pulled up their palisades and crossed the frontier moat. Huaimin entered Baodingchuan Fort. The enemy destroyed the plank bridge, cut off his retreat, made twenty-four separate crossings to pass their army through, and surrounded him.

sentences.zh: 又絕定川水泉上流，以饑渴其眾。

translations.literal: They also cut off the upper reaches of the Dingchuan springs to starve and thirst his troops.
translations.idiomatic: They also cut off the upper reaches of the Dingchuan springs to starve and thirst his troops.

sentences.zh: 劉賀率蕃兵門於河西，不勝，餘眾潰去。

translations.literal: Liu He led tribal troops to block the gate on the west bank of the river but was defeated; the remaining force fled in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Liu He led tribal troops to block the gate on the west bank of the river but was defeated, and the remaining force fled in disorder.

sentences.zh: 懷敏為中軍屯塞門東偏，英等陣東北隅。
