translations.literal: Huaimin stationed the central army on the eastern flank of Saimen; Ying and the others formed their line in the northeast corner.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin stationed the central army on the eastern flank of Saimen, while Ying and the others formed their line in the northeast corner.

sentences.zh: 敵自褊江三、葉燮會出，四面環之。

translations.literal: The enemy emerged under Bian Jiang, San, and Ye Xiehui and surrounded them on all four sides.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy emerged under the command of Bian Jiang, San, and Ye Xiehui and surrounded them on all four sides.

sentences.zh: 先以銳兵衝中軍，不動，回擊英軍。

translations.literal: First they sent elite troops to charge the central army; it did not move; they turned and struck Ying's army.
translations.idiomatic: First they sent elite troops to charge the central army, which held firm. They then turned and struck Ying's army.

sentences.zh: 會黑風起東北，部伍相失，陣遂擾。

translations.literal: Just then a black wind rose from the northeast; units lost contact with one another and the formation was thrown into disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Just then a black wind rose from the northeast. Units lost contact with one another and the formation collapsed into disorder.

sentences.zh: 士卒攀城堞爭入，英面被流矢，仆壕中，懷敏部兵見之亦奔駭。

translations.literal: Soldiers scrambled up the battlements to get inside; Ying was struck in the face by a flying arrow and fell into the moat; Huaimin's troops, seeing this, also fled in panic.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers scrambled up the battlements to get inside. Ying was struck in the face by a flying arrow and fell into the moat. Huaimin's troops, seeing this, also fled in panic.

sentences.zh: 懷敏為眾蹂躪幾死，輿致甕城，久之乃蘇。

translations.literal: Huaimin was nearly trampled to death by the crowd and was carried into the barbican; only after a long time did he revive.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin was nearly trampled to death in the chaos and was carried into the barbican. Only after a long time did he revive.

sentences.zh: 復選士據門橋，揮手刃以拒入城者。

translations.literal: He again selected men to hold the gate bridge and waved his blade to repel those trying to enter the city.
translations.idiomatic: He again selected men to hold the gate bridge and waved his blade to repel those trying to force their way into the city.

sentences.zh: 趙珣等以騎軍四合禦敵，敵眾稍卻，然大軍無鬥志。

translations.literal: Zhao Xun and others with cavalry closed in from four sides to resist the enemy; the enemy force retreated slightly, but the main army had no will to fight.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xun and others closed in with cavalry from four sides to resist the enemy. The enemy force retreated slightly, but the main army had lost all will to fight.

sentences.zh: 珣馳入，勸懷敏還軍中。

translations.literal: Xun galloped in and urged Huaimin to return to the army.
translations.idiomatic: Xun galloped in and urged Huaimin to return to the army.

sentences.zh: 是夕，敵聚火圍城四隅，臨西北呼曰：「爾得非總管廳點陣圖者邪？

translations.literal: That evening the enemy gathered fires around the four corners of the city and called from the northwest: "Are you not the one who drew up battle formations at the commander's hall?"
translations.idiomatic: That evening the enemy gathered fires around the four corners of the city and called from the northwest: "Are you not the one who drew up battle formations at the commander's hall?"

sentences.zh: 爾固能軍，乃入我圍中，今復何往！

translations.literal: "You claim to know how to command an army, yet you walked into our encirclement—where can you go now!"
translations.idiomatic: "You claim to know how to command an army, yet you walked straight into our encirclement. Where can you go now!"

sentences.zh: 」夜四鼓，懷敏召曹英、趙珣、李知和、王保、王文、許思純、劉賀、李良臣、趙瑜計議，莫知所出，遂謀結陣走鎮戎軍。

translations.literal: At the fourth watch of the night Huaimin summoned Cao Ying, Zhao Xun, Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, Wang Wen, Xu Sichun, Liu He, Li Liangchen, and Zhao Yu to deliberate; none knew what to do; they then planned to form up and retreat to Zhenrong Army.
translations.idiomatic: At the fourth watch of the night Huaimin summoned Cao Ying, Zhao Xun, Li Zhihe, Wang Bao, Wang Wen, Xu Sichun, Liu He, Li Liangchen, and Zhao Yu to deliberate. None knew what to do, and they planned to form up and retreat to Zhenrong Army.

sentences.zh: 雞鳴，懷敏自諭：「親軍左右及在後者皆毋得動，平明，從吾往安西堡。

translations.literal: At cockcrow Huaimin announced himself: "The personal guard on my left and right and those in the rear must not move; at daybreak follow me to Anxi Fort."
translations.idiomatic: At cockcrow Huaimin announced: "The personal guard on my left and right and those in the rear must not move. At daybreak follow me to Anxi Fort."

sentences.zh: 以英、珣為先鋒，賀、思純為左右翼，知和為殿，聽中軍鼓乃得行。

translations.literal: Ying and Xun shall be the vanguard, He and Sichun the left and right wings, Zhihe the rearguard; none may move until the central army drum sounds.
translations.idiomatic: Ying and Xun shall be the vanguard, He and Sichun the left and right wings, and Zhihe the rearguard. None may move until the central army drum sounds.

sentences.zh: 」至卯，鼓未作，懷敏先上馬，而大軍按堵未動。

translations.literal: By the mao hour the drum had not sounded; Huaimin mounted his horse first, while the main army remained still in ranks.
translations.idiomatic: By the mao hour the drum had not sounded. Huaimin mounted his horse first, while the main army remained still in ranks.

sentences.zh: 懷敏周麾者再，將徑去，有執鞚者勸不可，懷敏不得已而還。

translations.literal: Huaimin waved his command baton twice and was about to ride off directly; someone holding his bridle urged him not to; Huaimin had no choice but to return.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin waved his command baton twice and was about to ride off on his own. Someone holding his bridle urged him not to, and Huaimin had no choice but to return.

sentences.zh: 使參謀郭京等取芻城中，未至，懷敏復上馬，叱執轡者使去，不聽，拔劍且擊之，士遂散。

translations.literal: He sent staff officer Guo Jing and others to fetch fodder inside the city; before they arrived Huaimin mounted again, shouted at those holding his reins to let go; when they would not, he drew his sword and struck at them; the troops then scattered.
translations.idiomatic: He sent staff officer Guo Jing and others to fetch fodder inside the city. Before they returned Huaimin mounted again and shouted at those holding his reins to let go. When they would not, he drew his sword and struck at them, and the troops scattered.

sentences.zh: 懷敏驅馬東南馳二百里，至長城壕，路已斷，敵周圍之，遂與諸將皆遇害。

translations.literal: Huaimin spurred his horse southeast for two hundred li to the Great Wall moat; the road was already cut off; the enemy surrounded him, and he and the various generals were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin spurred his horse southeast for two hundred li to the Great Wall moat. The road was already cut off, the enemy surrounded him, and he and the various generals were all killed.

sentences.zh: 餘軍九千四百餘人，馬六百餘匹，為敵所斷。

translations.literal: The remaining army of more than nine thousand four hundred men and more than six hundred horses was cut down by the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: More than nine thousand four hundred remaining troops and more than six hundred horses were cut down by the enemy.

sentences.zh: 其子宗晟與趙正、郭京、承受王昭明等還保定川。

translations.literal: His son Zongcheng, together with Zhao Zheng, Guo Jing, Attendant Wang Zhaoming, and others, returned to Baodingchuan.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zongcheng, together with Zhao Zheng, Guo Jing, attendant Wang Zhaoming, and others, returned to Baodingchuan.

sentences.zh: 初，懷敏令軍中步兵毋得動，及前陣已去，後軍多不知者，故皆得存。

translations.literal: Initially Huaimin had ordered the infantry in the army not to move; when the forward ranks had already departed, many in the rear ranks did not know and therefore all survived.
translations.idiomatic: Initially Huaimin had ordered the infantry not to move. When the forward ranks had already departed, many in the rear ranks did not know and therefore survived.

sentences.zh: 時韓質、郝從政、胡息以兵六千保蓮華堡，劉湛、向進兵一千保向家峽，皆不赴援。

translations.literal: At the time Han Zhi, Hao Congzheng, and Hu Xi with six thousand troops held Lianhua Fort, and Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin with one thousand troops held Xiangjia Gorge; none came to reinforce.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Han Zhi, Hao Congzheng, and Hu Xi with six thousand troops held Lianhua Fort, and Liu Zhan and Xiang Jin with one thousand troops held Xiangjia Gorge. None came to reinforce.

sentences.zh: 於是敵長驅抵渭州，幅員六七百里，焚蕩廬舍，屠掠民畜而去。

translations.literal: Thereupon the enemy drove straight to Weizhou, sweeping an area six or seven hundred li across, burning dwellings, slaughtering and plundering people and livestock, and departing.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the enemy drove straight to Weizhou, sweeping an area six or seven hundred li across, burning dwellings, slaughtering and plundering people and livestock before departing.

sentences.zh: 奏至，帝嗟悼久之，贈懷敏鎮戎軍節度使兼太尉，英、知和、珣、保、文、質、嶽、貴、璘、思純、良臣及同時戰沒者，及涇原巡檢楊遵、籠竿城巡檢姚奭、涇原都巡檢司監押董謙、同巡檢唐斌、指使霍達，皆贈官有差。

translations.literal: When the memorial arrived, the emperor sighed in grief for a long time; Huaimin was posthumously granted the title of Military Governor of Zhenrong Army and concurrently Grand Preceptor; Ying, Zhihe, Xun, Bao, Wen, Zhi, Yue, Gui, Lin, Sichun, Liangchen, and those who fell in battle at the same time, as well as Jingyuan Inspector Yang Zun, Longgan City Inspector Yao Shi, Jingyuan Overall Inspection Office Supervisor Dong Qian, Co-Inspector Tang Bin, and Adjutant Huo Da, were all posthumously granted offices in varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: When the memorial arrived, the emperor sighed in grief for a long time. Huaimin was posthumously granted the title of military governor of Zhenrong Army and concurrently Grand Preceptor. Ying, Zhihe, Xun, Bao, Wen, Zhi, Yue, Gui, Lin, Sichun, Liangchen, and those who fell in battle at the same time, as well as Jingyuan inspector Yang Zun, Longgan City inspector Yao Shi, Jingyuan overall inspection office supervisor Dong Qian, co-inspector Tang Bin, and adjutant Huo Da, were all posthumously granted offices in varying degrees.

sentences.zh: 復降向進等官，落郝從政、趙瑜職。

translations.literal: Xiang Jin and others were again demoted in rank; Hao Congzheng and Zhao Yu were stripped of their posts.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Jin and others were demoted in rank, and Hao Congzheng and Zhao Yu were stripped of their posts.

sentences.zh: 懷敏通時事，善候人情，故多以才薦之。

translations.literal: Huaimin was versed in current affairs and skilled at reading people's sentiments; therefore many recommended him as talented.
translations.idiomatic: Huaimin was versed in current affairs and skilled at reading people's sentiments, and therefore many recommended him as talented.

sentences.zh: 及用為將，而輕率昧於應變，遂至覆軍。

translations.literal: When he was employed as a general, he was rash and ignorant of adapting to circumstances, and thus brought about the destruction of his army.
translations.idiomatic: When he was employed as a general, he proved rash and incapable of adapting to circumstances, and thus brought about the destruction of his army.

sentences.zh: 帝念之，賜諡忠隱。

translations.literal: The emperor remembered him and granted the posthumous name Zhongyin (Loyal and Retiring).
translations.idiomatic: The emperor remembered him fondly and granted the posthumous name Zhongyin, "Loyal and Retiring."

sentences.zh: 子宗晟、宗壽、宗禮、宗師，皆遷官。

translations.literal: His sons Zongcheng, Zongshou, Zongli, and Zongshi were all promoted in rank.
translations.idiomatic: His sons Zongcheng, Zongshou, Zongli, and Zongshi were all promoted in rank.

sentences.zh: 論曰：真宗澶淵之役，高瓊之功亦盛矣。

translations.literal: The commentary says: In Emperor Zhenzong's Chanyuan campaign, Gao Qiong's achievements were also great.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In Emperor Zhenzong's Chanyuan campaign, Gao Qiong's achievements were also considerable.

sentences.zh: 范廷召年十八，能手刃父仇；

translations.literal: Fan Tingzhao at eighteen could personally slay his father's enemy;
translations.idiomatic: Fan Tingzhao at eighteen could personally slay his father's enemy;

sentences.zh: 瓊將磔於市，幸以逃免；

translations.literal: Qiong was to be dismembered in the market and fortunately escaped;
translations.idiomatic: Qiong was sentenced to public dismemberment and fortunately escaped;

sentences.zh: 葛霸善擊刺馬射，給事藩邸，皆非素習韜略者也，及其出身戎行，迭居節鎮，而卓有可觀，由所遇之得其時也。

translations.literal: Ge Ba was skilled in thrusting, riding, and shooting and served at the princely residence—all were not by nature versed in military strategy; yet when they entered military service and successively held frontier commands, their accomplishments were notably worthy, because the times they encountered were favorable.
translations.idiomatic: Ge Ba was skilled in close combat, horsemanship, and archery and had served at the princely residence—none of them were by nature versed in military strategy. Yet when they entered military service and successively held frontier commands, their accomplishments were notably worthy, because the times they encountered were favorable.

sentences.zh: 或謂瓊頗自用，謀議不及參佐，而洞曉軍政；

translations.literal: Some say Qiong was rather self-willed and did not consult his staff in planning, yet was thoroughly versed in military affairs;
translations.idiomatic: Some say Qiong was rather self-willed and did not consult his staff in planning, yet was thoroughly versed in military affairs;

sentences.zh: 霸雖失於巽懦，而能謹直自持；

translations.literal: Ba, though failing through timidity and weakness, was able to maintain scrupulous integrity;
translations.idiomatic: Ba, though failing through timidity, was able to maintain scrupulous integrity;

sentences.zh: 廷召性雖癖，在軍中四十年，累從征討，所至有功：皆不害其為驍果也。

translations.literal: Tingzhao's nature, though eccentric, did not prevent his being fierce and resolute: in the army for forty years, repeatedly following campaigns, wherever he went he achieved merit.
translations.idiomatic: Tingzhao's nature, though eccentric, did not prevent his being fierce and resolute: in forty years of army service, repeatedly following campaigns, wherever he went he achieved merit.

sentences.zh: 廷召諸子，珪為最賢，霸子懷敏以戰死，固皆足稱。

translations.literal: Among Tingzhao's sons, Gui was the most worthy; Ba's son Huaimin died in battle—all are indeed worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: Among Tingzhao's sons, Gui was the most worthy; Ba's son Huaimin died in battle—all are indeed worthy of praise.

sentences.zh: 若繼宣、繼勳之將業，則過其父遠甚，此「克勤敏功鍾慶之碑」所由以立歟！

translations.literal: As for Jixuan and Jixun's military achievements, they far surpassed their father—was this not why the stele "Meritorious Diligence Bringing Accumulated Blessings" was erected!
translations.idiomatic: As for the military achievements of Jixuan and Jixun, they far surpassed their father—is this not why the stele "Meritorious Diligence Bringing Accumulated Blessings" was erected!

sentences.zh: 夫以三子之自樹如此，而不得與狄青、郭逵同日而論者，豈非拳勇之有餘，而器識之不足也歟！

translations.literal: That these three sons achieved such standing on their own yet cannot be discussed on the same day as Di Qing and Guo Kui—is this not because they had more than enough raw courage but insufficient breadth of vision and judgment!
translations.idiomatic: That these three sons achieved such standing on their own yet cannot be ranked alongside Di Qing and Guo Kui—is this not because they had more than enough raw courage but insufficient breadth of vision and judgment!
